subject: Post-call: Arcadia Payments — cost levers, deployment criteria, next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Gonzalez <carlos.gonzalez@arcadiapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Arcadia Payments — cost levers, deployment criteria, next steps

Hi Carlos — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations.

Key pain points you shared
- Embeddings and vector search are the largest monthly line items today — heavy fanout for similarity scoring (~4–5 lookups per query).
- Peak-hour chat volume spikes create p95 latency concerns for support flows; SLA target you mentioned was ~150ms p95 for short completions.
- Tight procurement/budget window: current FY22 budget for this initiative is constrained to a mid-five-figure monthly cap unless we can demonstrate immediate unit-cost reductions.

Goals we heard
- Reduce per-1M-token cost for embedding+search flows by ~30–50% within a pilot.
- Preserve output quality (no regression on top-5 retrievals).
- Prove operational fit (latency SLOs, predictable billing) before committing to reserved capacity.

Primary levers we discussed (short form)
- Batching + affinity routing: combine inference requests to increase GPU utilization; expected token-cost reduction depends on request shape but typically 20–35% for your traffic profile.
- Prefix/KV caching for chat/common prompts: large wins for repeat prompts and shorter context reuse (est. additional 10–25% savings).
- Quantization / smaller model tier for lower-priority workloads: 15–30% tradeoff with minimal quality loss on retrieval tasks if we validate.
- Serving topology: Hosted + burst into Dedicated vs Dedicated-only — tradeoffs for cost predictability vs time-to-value.

Pilot proposal (3-week technical pilot) — what we'd aim to validate
- Scope: production-ish slice (1–2M tokens/day peak, ~12M total tokens) covering support chat + embedding refresh flow.
- Success criteria: >=30% net unit-cost reduction with <5% quality regressions on retrievals, maintain p95 <200ms for chat flows.
- Deliverables: cost workbook with per-1M-token scenarios, dashboard access (latency & token breakdown), ops runbook for rollout.

Asks from Arcadia
- Confirm the budget guardrail (you mentioned an internal cap) and target monthly spend ceiling.
- Introduce engineering contact(s) for a short technical kickoff (30–45m) next week.
- Any procurement constraints for trial (PO required, security questionnaire, beatable terms)?

Attached: arcadia-cost-workbook.xlsx (token scenarios) and pilot-sow-draft.docx (draft SOW). I added rough per-1M-token rows so you can see Hosted vs Dedicated delta.

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm budget cap and whether procurement needs a PO or vendor packet (EoD Wed).
2) If ok, schedule technical kickoff with Marissa (solutions engineering) and Ben (TAM) — I can provide 3 times.
3) We'll lock pilot scope and send a one-page pilot SOW for signatures.

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed any nuance.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Post-call: Arcadia Payments — cost levers, deployment criteria, next steps

Thanks Priya — really helpful recap. A few clarifying items from my side: 

1) Budget: our sponsor has signaled we can move forward with a pilot if we can keep month-1 exposed spend under $45k (that includes any third-party infra costs). Is your 3-week pilot likely to stay within that bound for the profile you proposed?

2) Per-1M-token estimate: can you give a ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated delta per 1M tokens (so I can short-list to procurement)? A single-line estimate is fine.

3) Procurement: we do require a vendor packet (W-9/insurance) and in some cases an initial PO for pilots. Procurement is looped here — procurement@arcadiapay.com will advise on required docs.

4) Security: we may need a short answers summary to our security questionnaire (SOC2 scope, data residency, access controls). Can you confirm the right contact at Redwood to drive that?

If those checks look OK I'm optimistic we can book the technical kickoff this week. I'll aim to get procurement's list by EOD Tuesday.

— Carlos
Carlos Gonzalez

Carlos — thanks for the quick reply and the budget ceiling callout, very helpful. Short answers below and a couple of concrete next steps.

1) Budget fit (ballpark)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) — rough baseline: $3,800 per 1M tokens for the mixed workload we discussed (embeddings + chat).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, amortized) — approx $2,300 per 1M tokens for steady-state usage once you reach sustained volume and enable batching/caching.
- Pilot estimate (3 weeks, 12M tokens): Hosted path likely ~ $46k gross; with batching/caching optimizations applied during pilot we model ~30% savings (so net ~ $32k). Dedicated-only pilot costs depend on committed capacity; we usually do hybrid: Hosted baseline + short Dedicated burst to validate tail latencies.

Notes: these are directional until we instrument a small sample of traffic — the workbook I attached has scenario rows (no complex math, just multiplier assumptions).

2) Security / procurement contacts
- For security questionnaire: Marissa Cole (solutions engineering) will pick this up and can provide SOC2 summary + KMS/HSM details. Marissa: can you prepare a 1–2 page answer set for Arcadia's questionnaire?
- Procurement: Ben Carter (TAM) will coordinate vendor packet and initial PO flow. Ben: looping you so you can flag any red lines.

3) Proposed near-term calendar
- Tech kickoff: 30–45m with Marissa + Ben — I have availability Wed 24th 10:00–11:00 PT, Thu 25th 13:00–14:00 PT, Fri 26th 08:30–09:15 PT. Please pick one or propose a different slot.
- We'll produce a one-page pilot SOW and an updated cost workbook (per-1M-token rows + Hosted vs Dedicated delta) after the technical kickoff.

4) Attachments and next artifacts
- Attached: arcadia-cost-workbook.xlsx (updated with per-1M rows) and pilot-sow-draft.docx (lightweight SOW you can circulate).
- I'll also create a short HubSpot record and share links after you confirm the slot.

If procurement needs any vendor paperwork up front, Ben will handle it. Carlos — appreciate the runway on procurement and the candid budget cap; we'll aim to design the pilot to hit that $45k exposure target as closely as possible.

Best —
Priya
